top3.headline: Amodei and Dimon go live as Anthropic's IPO moves ahead
top3.whyItMatters: Anthropic now pitches under IPO rules, so its public claims carry securities-law weight.

top3.headline: LangChain raises $300M at a $3B valuation
top3.whyItMatters: Over 7,000 companies run agents on LangSmith; check lock-in before your stack standardizes.

top3.headline: Vercel's Workflow SDK 5 targets faster, safer agent runs
top3.whyItMatters: Durable workflow runtimes are becoming the default way to run long agent jobs reliably.

items.title: Rauch: Workflow SDK 5 makes Vercel agent steps faster
items.takeaway: He claims faster time to first step and between steps, plus stronger encryption and security.
items.soWhat: Durable workflow runtimes are becoming the default way to run long agent jobs reliably.

items.title: LangChain raises $300M at a $3B valuation
items.takeaway: LangChain says more than 7,000 companies use LangSmith for agent runtime, improvement and governance.
items.soWhat: Agent tooling vendors are scaling fast; check lock-in before your agent stack standardizes on one.

items.title: Dario Amodei sits down live with JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon
items.takeaway: Anthropic streamed the fireside at 12 PM ET; the post carries its SEC registration notice for the offering.
items.soWhat: Anthropic is now pitching in public under IPO rules, so its claims carry securities-law weight.

image.alt: @AnthropicAI on X: Dario Amodei sits down live with JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon

items.title: Wiz CTO: AI runs in 20 minutes attacks that took weeks
items.takeaway: Ami Luttwak says companies must keep attacking their own systems with the latest models.
items.soWhat: Budget for continuous AI red-teaming; yearly penetration tests no longer match attacker speed.

items.title: Meng To shares the skills behind his product demos
items.takeaway: dream-loop pairs Blender and image generation with a critic agent; Hairline draws pointer-aware isometric lines.
items.soWhat: Design teams can package their demo craft as reusable agent skills.

items.title: Matt Pocock builds skills that turn work into short videos
items.takeaway: /setup-animatic sets up tooling; /animatic makes an upload-ready video. Both are in progress.
items.soWhat: Video walkthroughs may replace long markdown write-ups when reviewing agent-built work.

items.title: Meng To: Fable 5.2 builds a three.js game under 10 MB
items.takeaway: A Japanese-inspired FPS on his sakura valley scene, in HTML with no image or model files.
items.soWhat: Playable prototypes now fit in one file; design reviews can start from working demos.

items.title: Peter Steinberger's team writes up OpenAI's persistent agents
items.takeaway: He says his team wrote about how they run persistent agents inside OpenAI; his post links the write-up.
items.soWhat: A frontier lab's own operating notes are a rare benchmark for your agent setup.

items.title: Simon Willison: Gemini 4 Carbon and Argon prices double Dec 1
items.takeaway: Argon and Carbon share one token price; the new Hydrogen is only a 25% discount on it.
items.soWhat: Teams running agents on Gemini 4 should re-cost those workloads before December.

items.title: Perplexity open-sources Decider v1.3 decision models
items.takeaway: Decider v1.3 and Decider Flash v1.3 add a 'locate' capability and are free on OpenRouter for a week.
items.soWhat: Small open decision models are a cheap option for routing and classification inside agents.

items.title: Replit Agent can now buy ads for your business
items.takeaway: Replit's CEO says users can ask the agent to make purchases, including ads to acquire customers.
items.soWhat: Agents now spend company money; set budgets, approvals and audit trails before turning this on.

items.title: Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips against smuggling
items.takeaway: MIT Technology Review reports the private confirmation came while the industry publicly questioned the idea.
items.soWhat: Tracking is feasible, so export rules could require it; watch your AI hardware supply.

image.alt: Image from MIT Tech Review AI

items.title: Anthropic puts Claude inside your team's video calls
items.takeaway: Claude Meetings joins video calls and builds docs and whiteboards live; beta on Team and Enterprise plans.
items.soWhat: Meetings become a source of agent context; set rules for what Claude may hear and keep.

items.title: Ray Dalio: let someone else measure your progress
items.takeaway: Ideally someone other than you measures and reports your progress; missed targets are a separate problem to diagnose.
items.soWhat: Independent measurement keeps leaders honest; assign it outside the team that owns the target.

items.title: Google ships Gemini 4 Hydrogen, built for speed
items.takeaway: Google says it finishes tasks 2.5x faster than 3.8 Flash and beats Argon on an intelligence index.
items.soWhat: Fast, cheaper models keep improving; retest your default model for everyday agent work.

items.title: Claude Managed Agents can now run in your own cloud
items.takeaway: Private beta: host the agent harness, sandboxes and session history on your cloud or on-premises.
items.soWhat: Regulated teams can run Anthropic's agents while keeping data and logs inside their walls.

items.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, effective immediately
items.takeaway: Nvidia's newsroom announced a CEO transition; Reuters live coverage reports Huang resigned immediately.
items.soWhat: Your biggest AI supplier changes leaders mid-boom; watch for shifts in pricing, roadmap and allocation.

items.title: Anthropic files its IPO registration with the SEC
items.takeaway: Anthropic says it has filed a registration statement, including a prospectus, for its initial public offering.
items.soWhat: A public Anthropic will disclose costs and risks; read the prospectus before your next model contract.

items.title: Naval: someone, somewhere, will build the datacenters
items.takeaway: He calls datacenters a globally competitive market and says someone, somewhere, will build them.
items.soWhat: Compute supply is global; local limits shift where capacity lands, not whether it exists.

items.title: United won't let unauthorized AI agents book flights
items.takeaway: The Verge reports United is refusing bookings made by unauthorized AI agents.
items.soWhat: Agent access is now a business decision; check which partners will block your customer-facing agents.

items.title: Lyn Alden: wary of Huang's tenure, bullish on 2027 GPU demand
items.takeaway: She calls herself neutral to bearish on Huang as CEO and bullish on GPU demand in 2027.
items.soWhat: A respected macro voice separates Nvidia's leadership risk from the demand for AI compute.
